Title: One store records every event of the new layer, read with plain queries

## For the human
- **What:** в новом репо orch-it появляется общее хранилище событий слоя: каждое событие любой роли, любой машины и любой ОС пишется в него одной строкой, а любой вопрос о работе слоя (сколько стоил тикет, кто сколько ждал, какие навыки вызваны) отвечается одним запросом к нему; первым туда попадает расход денег и токенов каждой сессии Claude, прочитанный из её журнала.
- **Goal:** владелец и мозг видят все события работы слоя в одном месте и разбирают поломки и расходы по нему, а не новыми ручными замерами; ни одно событие из утверждённого списка не требует потом переделки хранилища.
- **Plan:** один сильный агент с помощниками строит хранилище по утверждённому списку событий (форма записи, проверка каждого события, запросы), первым источником делает журналы сессий Claude, заводит в orch-it словарь и первое архитектурное решение; каждая часть вливается через пулл-реквест, зелёный на Linux и Windows.
- **Result:** 100 % видов событий и шагов из утверждённого списка (47 видов, 23 шага) есть в хранилище; 0 потерянных и 0 порванных записей при 8 одновременных писателях на Linux и на Windows; повторная загрузка того же журнала добавляет 0 событий; запрос «цена тикета от готовности до закрытия по ролям» даёт суммы, равные посчитанным вручную; случай вне названных: события второй машины, скопированные в хранилище первой, сливаются без единого дубля; каждая стоимость модели Claude показана и в долларах, и в процентах недельного лимита подписки; в закрывающем комментарии — реальный расход самой этой части по сессиям и моделям, прочитанный из хранилища.
- **Undo:** two-way door (новый код в новом репо, старый слой не трогается; формат записи закрепляется решением, менять его позже дороже); touches только orch-it и папку хранилища на каждой машине, где он стоит.

## For the agent

Weight: 8

Step: part 1 of the rebuild order (#387 resolution, comment 6398337229): "the event store and the record's skeleton". Waits on part 0 (#392, done: orch-it, `main` takes only a PR green on the `linux` and `windows` jobs) and the event list (#388, done). Driver: one strong agent with helpers (#376, #387 "Driver"): an Opus 5.5 high session in the orch-it checkout; the store's format and validation are the strong agent's own units, the importer, CLI and tests may go to Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 helpers. The old repo is read only as a source of cases, never copied (#387).

The owner's purpose for the store (#387 owner-answer comment): every event of every link visible and easy to analyse, so the layer's work is read and fixed from the store, never by a new hand measurement.

### The list it is built to

The event list of #388 and its section 8 (#389), on the never-merged branch `research/event-list-355` of this repo, file `docs/research/2026-10-25-event-list-355.md`: the envelope (section 2), 23 step ids (17 in section 3, 6 in section 8), 47 point kinds (45 in section 4, `step.progressed`, `machine.resumed`), the outcome set `passed`, `failed`, `no_result`, `refused`, `lost`, `stopped`, and every reason-code list written next to its field. Kinds, envelope, outcomes and reason codes are closed; a step's or kind's `detail` is open (a writer adds a field without a store change).

### Decided by the brain (with reasons)

1. **Write format: append-only JSON Lines, one file per writer.** Each writing process appends to its own file `<store>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<writer-id>.jsonl`, one event per line, flushed per line. Reason: no lock and no server on any OS, a crashed writer loses at most its last line, and two machines' stores merge by copying files (union by `id`). Rejected: one shared SQLite file as the write target (a file lock across processes, Windows locking, no merge across machines); a hosted database (an account and a secret for every stranger who installs the layer, against "works anywhere", map #355 Notes).
2. **Read side: a SQLite index built from the files**, stdlib `sqlite3` with JSON functions, one table `events` with the envelope as columns and `detail` as JSON (so section 7's query runs as written). The index is a cache: deleting it and rebuilding gives the same rows; it reads new lines incrementally and skips a half-written last line until it is complete.
3. **Where the store lives:** a setting, default the per-user data folder of the OS (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\orch-it\events` on Windows, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/orch-it/events` or `~/.local/share/orch-it/events` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/orch-it/events` on macOS). One store per machine for every repo on it; the `repo` field separates them. A store folder inside a git work tree is refused (events never reach a commit, so never a public copy).
4. **The closed sets live in one machine-readable file in the package**, the only place a kind, step id, outcome or reason code is defined; validation reads it; `docs/events.md` in orch-it is the human list and a test checks the two agree both ways. Validation raises on a closed-set breach (CODING_STANDARDS: a function returns a result or raises); the error carries a code, never prose to parse.
5. **Event ids:** time-ordered random for a live writer; for an event imported from a source record, a hash of (source, record id, kind), so a re-import writes nothing new.
6. **`turn.used` is read from the session's Claude Code transcript** (the question #388 left open). Reason: the transcript exists for every launch form (desktop chat, headless, subagent), while the headless JSON total exists only for headless runs. Per assistant message id once (a message split over several transcript lines counts once); subagent transcripts are their own `subagent` sessions with `parent_session` set. Prices from a price file in the package with source and date per model, tiers and the 1-hour cache write included (the old table `config/model_prices.json` of this repo is the source of the numbers and the tier rule); a model missing from the price file writes `usd: null` with reason `price_missing`, never a guessed price.
7. **The first writer is the transcript importer:** from a transcript folder it writes `session` and `subagent` step pairs, `turn.used`, `tool.called` (`args_head` at most 120 characters) and `skill.called`. Every other kind gets its writer in the part that owns it.
8. **CLI:** `python -m orch_it events import <transcript folder>`, `events query "<sql>"`, and named queries `ticket-cost` (section 7 of the list, as written there), `session-cost` ($, % week and tokens per session and model, subagents under their parent) and `limit-rate` (decision 9).
9. **Cost as a share of the weekly subscription limit** (owner, 2026-10-25: "стоимость дополнительно считать в % лимита у макс подписки клод если модель клод? недельного лимита"). Every cost a query prints for a Claude model shows `% week` beside the dollars: usd / the setting `weekly_limit_usd_per_pct` (dollars at API prices per 1 % of the weekly limit, with the plan's name and the date it was measured). The setting has no built-in number (it differs per plan and changes when the limits change): unset, the column prints `not set`, never a guess; this installation's first value is the old layer's reading, 16.5 (`config/orchestration.json:29` of this repo, card at 26 % on 2026-10-24 21:14). A reading of the usage card is recorded as `value.measured` (`name` `weekly_limit_pct`, `unit` `%`) by `events measure-limit <pct>`; the named query `limit-rate` gives dollars per 1 % between two readings from the `turn.used` sums between them, so the setting is re-read from the store when the limits change. A non-Claude model's cost prints `% week` as `n/a`.
10. **The record's skeleton in orch-it** (#387 part 1, area 12): `GLOSSARY.md` with only the words this part uses (event, kind, envelope, step pair, outcome, reason code, detail, store, index, writer), and `docs/adr/0001` for decisions 1-6 and 9 (the write format is hard to reverse). Nothing of the old `GLOSSARY.md` or ADRs is copied (#382: 44 of 88 terms name removed parts).

### Sources read as cases (never copied)

- Transcript readers of the old layer: `scripts/token_meter.py`, `scripts/own_turns.py`, `tools/agentops/outcomes.py`, `tools/replays/c_run.py` (how usage, message ids and subagent files are read today, and their known misses).
- Price rules: `config/model_prices.json` (its `_comment` states the 1-hour write and tier rules).
- A real transcript to try on: any file under the user's `~/.claude/projects/<project>/` folder; the brain's chat of 2026-10-25 18:35-18:58 (61 turns, Opus 5.5, $2.92 by the old table) is a known sample to compare with.

### Acceptance

| row | check | pass |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the closed sets against #388 sections 2, 3, 4, 8 | all 23 step ids, all 47 point kinds, the 6 outcomes, every reason-code list present; the doc/file agreement test fails on a planted extra kind in either one |
| 2 | refusals | an unknown kind, an outcome outside the set, a reason code outside its list, a missing envelope field, an `at` without a zone: each raises with its own code; an unknown `detail` field is accepted and queryable |
| 3 | concurrent writers, in the `linux` and the `windows` job | 8 processes writing 1000 events each at once: the index holds 8000, 0 torn lines, 0 duplicate ids |
| 4 | transcript import | tokens per model of a fixture transcript equal its hand sum exactly; the same transcript imported twice: the second run adds 0 events; a transcript whose last line is half written: no error, that line lands on the next run |
| 5 | missing price | a turn of a model absent from the price file: `usd` null with `price_missing`, no number |
| 6 | `ticket-cost` | on a fixture with a ticket's ready edit, its close, a direct turn and a turn shared by two held tickets: per-role sums equal the fixture's hand values, the shared turn split and marked `shared` |
| 7 | outside case: a second machine | machine B's store files copied into machine A's store: the index holds A + B with 0 duplicate ids (an event present on both counts once), and `session-cost` reads both machines |
| 8 | store inside a git work tree | refused with its code before any write |
| 9 | the owner-visible result | `session-cost` over this part's own sessions (the driver and its helpers) posted in the closing comment, $, % week and tokens per session and model, minutes as minutes |
| 10 | % of the weekly limit | with the setting at 16.5, a fixture turn of $2.92 prints 0.18 % week; with it unset, `not set`; a non-Claude model, `n/a`; two `weekly_limit_pct` readings 10 % and 12 % with $33 of `turn.used` between them: `limit-rate` gives 16.5 |
| 11 | how it lands | every unit a PR to orch-it merged green on `linux` and `windows`; each diff reviewed on the Standards, Spec and edge-input axes (#381) with findings and fixes counted; report lines `tdd`, `codebase-design`, `domain-modeling` per the skill table |

Outside case: events written on a second machine and copied into the first machine's store (row 7): the six sources and this ticket's other rows all write on one machine; a store that keys events by file or by line number, or trusts one writer per store, double-counts or loses them.
Same object: Claude Code writes the transcripts while a session runs and the importer reads them, read-only: a half-written last line is skipped and read next run (row 4); the old layer's transcript readers (`scripts/token_meter.py`, `scripts/own_turns.py`, `tools/agentops/outcomes.py`) read the same files read-only too, so both run without effect on each other; the store folder is new and nothing in the old layer writes to it; orch-it's `main` protection (#392) is the only gate on landing.
Not in this ticket: every writer but the transcript importer (each comes with its part: test runs in part 2, guards in part 3, tickets and roles in part 4, PRs in part 5, the launcher in part 6); how events written on GitHub's machines reach a store (part 5, held to decision 1's merge by file copy); the monitor's views (part 7); orch-it's `CLAUDE.md`, role files and coding standards (part 4); labels or issues in orch-it.
